estimand: total greenhouse-gas emissions, in tCO2e, for reporting year 2024, of an illustrative office-based financial-services firm with offices in Frankfurt, Paris and Milan, by scope, with a 95% Monte Carlo interval

commute_days_per_year.rationale: euro-area working days net of annual leave and public holidays, rounded; a fully office-based firm is assumed (no structural WFH discount)

commute_distance_km_oneway.rationale: typical one-way commute for an office worker in a large euro-area city

business_travel_km_per_employee_year.rationale: moderately travel-intensive office role (client and inter-office travel), not a sales or field role

business_travel_air_share.rationale: even split between short-haul flights and rail for inter-city business travel within continental Europe; no basis to assume either dominates

gas_activity_uncertainty_pct.rationale: compounds a national sector average, an employment-based per-employee scaling and an assumed headcount -- three approximations stacked

elec_activity_uncertainty_pct.rationale: same chain of approximations as the gas activity figure

commute_travel_activity_uncertainty_pct.rationale: distance and mode split are themselves assumptions, not fitted to this firm

combustion_factor_uncertainty_pct.rationale: published national combustion factors are the least uncertain input in this inventory; treated as tight but not exact

grid_intensity_uncertainty_pct.rationale: set from the module's own validation against AIB's independently computed production-mix CO2 figure -- the divergence ranges from 3% (Germany) to over 100% (France, where CRF1A1A/GEP and AIB's Ecoinvent-based production mix disagree sharply); 30% is the largest of the three country divergences that is not the France outlier, used as a conservative single figure -- see results/emissions_inventory.json:validation

residual_mix_uncertainty_pct.rationale: AIB residual mix is a one-year snapshot; year-to-year movement of 10%+ is observed in the AIB series for several member states

completeness.name: Purchased goods and services
completeness.reason: no public spend-based emission-factor set is reachable with this module's library stack (stdlib, numpy, pandas, matplotlib, openpyxl only); likely the largest true gap for an office-based services firm (IT services, professional services, office supplies)

completeness.name: Capital goods
completeness.reason: no capex data for an illustrative firm and no generic public per-employee benchmark

completeness.name: Fuel- and energy-related activities
completeness.reason: WTT on Scope 1 gas and T&D losses on Scope 2 electricity, both computed from data already fetched for Scope 1/2

completeness.name: Upstream transportation and distribution
completeness.reason: not applicable -- a financial-services firm distributes no physical product

completeness.name: Waste generated in operations
completeness.reason: Eurostat publishes waste generation only at municipal aggregate level, not decomposable to a commercial-services employee; an office-waste-per-employee figure would be an unfetched assumption stacked on an unfetched assumption, one layer too many

completeness.name: Business travel
completeness.reason: assumed travel budget, split air/rail, DESNZ factors

completeness.name: Employee commuting
completeness.reason: assumed commute distance and frequency, Eurostat national modal split, DESNZ factors

completeness.name: Upstream leased assets
completeness.reason: the three offices are the firm's only leased assets and are already Scope 1/2 under the operational-control boundary this inventory uses

completeness.name: Downstream leased assets
completeness.reason: the firm leases no assets to others

completeness.name: Investments
completeness.reason: financed emissions -- excluded here by the roadmap and named as the reason for module 05

validation.source: AIB European Residual Mixes 2024, CO2 sheet, Production mix CO2 column -- independent of the Eurostat CRF1A1A/GEP ratio this module fits

order_of_magnitude_check.note: a wide sanity bound meant to catch a unit or scaling error, not a published per-employee benchmark
